page: Microsoft Azure M16ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on dedicated 64-bit ARM architecture. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance supplies 16 dedicated ARM vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an extensive memory ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU, targeting workloads that require significant working sets resident in system RAM.

The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage, operating purely as a diskless instance that relies on remote Premium Storage options for persistent disk volumes and operating system images. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual networking components for external egress and ingress.

Because the server combines a high 1:16 core-to-memory footprint with ARM-based architecture, it offers a resource-dense alternative to traditional x86 memory-heavy instances. It avoids the costs of integrated local NVMe drives while maximizing memory allocation per core, making it effective for in-memory caching layers, large relational database engines, and ARM-native enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure M16ps_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16 dedicated ARM vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of memory, resulting in a dense memory footprint of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle any local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on external Premium Storage for block device attachments. Networking does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Due to its ARM-based compute allocation and vast memory array, the M16ps_v4 provides an efficient resource profile for memory-bound tasks. It is configured primarily for large in-memory key-value databases, memory-resident analytic caches, enterprise relational databases, and data processing pipelines compiled for ARM64 environments.
